machineProject.name: USB mouse reuse study
machineProject.purpose: Develop a useful single-action USB foot control from an ordinary discarded wired mouse, without buying a development board. Compare alternatives and persist concrete engineering work; no physical specimen or measurements exist.

actions.action: Obtain actual donor identity, external condition, button positions and available reclaimed base/hinge/return materials. Report actual dimensions and provenance; do not import B100 envelope as specimen dimensions.

On a later authorized bench, establish enumeration and actual input reports; identify exactly one chosen button down/up pair and confirm release behavior. Capture OS/application and supported bindings.
Size an adjustable mouse cradle and independent pedal load path; set compliant pusher and positive stop using actual button force/travel evidence. No build dimensions established here.
Only if remote option remains needed, obtain unpowered switch-node continuity/topology evidence and reclaimed switch/wire/enclosure inventory before drawing any pin-level schematic.

Proposed later acceptance: 100 deliberate press/release cycles yield exactly 100 target actions and no extra events; 10-second hold yields one action then releases cleanly; no pointer/wheel/other-button events, slipping, cable pull or switch bottoming. These are proposed trial criteria, not lifetime proof or completed tests.
Retain this bounded plan until arbitrary mouse-controller and mechanical-only specs are supported or a measured donor contract exists. Do not repair into an invented catalog board to pass HS.

Implement and validate the recorded DISARMED/ARMED/HELD host behavior only after OS/application binding and device-identity evidence. Evaluate V1-V7 including bounce and connect-held handling; no software was implemented here.

Evaluate the recorded pedal_parameterization with actual donor tolerances, safe travel/force evidence and intended foot load before selecting dimensions. If safe bounds are unavailable, remain pending.

behavioral_contract.qualification: Require evidence-based stable down/release qualification if raw input chatters. No debounce interval is asserted from these documents. A bouncing release must not prematurely re-arm; timing must later balance chatter rejection and minimum intended inter-press interval.
behavioral_contract.reconnect: Do not replay queued clicks or infer release from unplugging. Reconnect/focus restoration requires released baseline and fresh press. Global-focus operation would require an explicit revised target requirement.
behavioral_contract.routing: Select donor by observed device identity with a reconnect policy; do not globally bind every mouse. Choose exactly one native-binding or remapper path so a physical press is not counted twice. If device isolation or repeat suppression is unavailable, the selected application path fails this requirement.
behavioral_contract.scope: Both candidates; host mapping or target application must provide this behavior without changing donor firmware.
behavioral_contract.startup: Start DISARMED; a device connected with button already held produces zero actions until released and deliberately pressed again.

pedal_parameterization.exemplar_limit: S1 dimensions 113x62x38 mm describe the B100 product envelope only and cannot fill any actual-donor variable.
feasibility: y_stop_min > g_max + x_on_max, with positive actuation margin
y_stop_max < g_min + x_safe_min, with positive overtravel margin
Released pusher must clear button despite return tolerances; verify complete button-up independently.

These inequalities require a nonempty tolerance window. If no safe travel bound or no feasible window exists, do not size a rigid pusher; redesign the compliant mechanism or reject this donor geometry.
pedal_parameterization.force_constraint: Travel inequalities do not prove safe force. The compliant pusher must independently cap force before the base stop bears foot load; measure required actuation force and establish a safe force bound. Do not infer a foot-load rating from a hand-operated mouse switch.
pedal_parameterization.load_path: At end travel, base/hinge/treadle stop must bypass mouse and switch. Define intended maximum foot load and examine stop, hinge, base, slip and pinch risks before any later build.

variables.g: pusher-to-button initial clearance, with tolerance interval [g_min,g_max]
variables.x_on: button displacement needed to actuate, worst-case x_on_max
variables.x_safe: independently established safe button displacement upper limit, conservative x_safe_min
variables.y_stop: pusher displacement at structural stop, tolerance interval [y_stop_min,y_stop_max]
